claims.text: Conventionally cast or laser-clad AlCoCrFeNi2.1 has a fine lamellar microstructure comprising FCC/L12 and BCC/B2 phases.
The conventionally processed alloy is not optimized for nanoscale precipitate strengthening and does not meet certain industrial performance criteria.
Heat treatment at about 900 °C can precipitate an Al-rich L12 phase within the FCC phase of AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
An optimized step-aging treatment can produce a fine, uniform, nanoscale distribution of Al-rich L12 precipitates in the FCC lamellae.
An inert treatment atmosphere will prevent unwanted oxidation.
Nanoscale L12 precipitates will pin dislocations.
Nanoscale L12 precipitates will pin grain boundaries and hinder grain-boundary sliding.
The L12 phase in AlCoCrFeNi2.1 has greater bending strength, strain hardening, and plastic deformation capacity than the B2 phase.
The L12 precipitate dispersion will improve resistance to deformation during long-term mechanical loading and temperature fluctuations.
The aging treatment will enhance the alloy's high-temperature stability.
The aging treatment will reduce room-temperature creep rates relative to the conventionally processed alloy.
The L12 precipitate dispersion will contribute to formation of a more stable and protective oxide scale.
The aged alloy will show improved corrosion resistance, including reduced oxide-scale spallation.
The aged alloy will have a superior strength-ductility balance relative to the conventionally processed alloy.
Heat treatment near 900 °C can cause grain growth in AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
Excessive aging may coarsen precipitates or grains and negate the proposed benefits.
The benefits depend on retaining the precipitates in the nanoscale regime.
The optimal aging time and temperature remain undetermined.
The long-term stability of the precipitates under cyclic temperature and mechanical loading remains undetermined.
